name: galaxy-tools: a real tool run lands as a loom-job block and the poller follows it
description: The Galaxy tools are galaxy-ops operations registered in-process under bare names. Capture keys and records the run under that bare name, and it reads the job ids from the wrapper's envelope (structuredContent, or the text when a handler rewrote the content). A change in either shows up here as a run that went through with nothing recorded. The agent stages a small BED file by URL, runs wc_gnu on it and waits for the result, so the session stays alive across poller ticks: the scenario asserts that the run_tool result came from the in-process wrapper (details.galaxy.tool), the submission.registered row under the bare name, the loom-job block in notebook.md, and a poll.transition row for the wc_gnu job reaching a terminal state. upload_file is hidden. The history is orbit-eval- prefixed for --galaxy-cleanup.
inputs: Create a new Galaxy history named exactly `orbit-eval-job-{{RUN_ID}}`. Upload this BED file into it by URL: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/galaxyproject/galaxy/release_24.0/test-data/1.bed . Then run the Galaxy tool `wc_gnu` (Line/Word/Character count) on that dataset with default settings. Wait until the wc_gnu job has finished -- check on it every so often -- and then tell me how many lines the BED file has according to the tool's output. Skip the formal plan; this is a quick check.
